text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALES - Turkey recently bought 28,000 tonnes of French soft wheat at $154 a tonne, FOB, grain exporters said. Shipments will be in June. The wheat is to be delivered from the 1996 old crop and must contain at least 12 pct protein.

- Sri Lanka bought 61,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat under Title 1 of the PL-480 programme. Sri Lanka bought one lot of 48,000 tonnes of wheat at $153.69 per tonne and another 13,000 tonnes at $154.60 per tonne for July delivery. The suppliers were Japan's Mitsubishi Corp and Marubeni Corp.

WHEAT SALES (cont.) - The Canadian Wheat Board sold 150,000 tonnes of milling wheat and 150,000 tonnes of durum wheat to Algeria, trade sources said. "They sold the durum at US$200 CIF Algeria for July-August delivery and they sold 150,000 of milling wheat for July, August, September shipments at US$159 CIF which is pretty low," one source said.

RICE SALE - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foodstuffs (GEZA) has bought 12,000 tonnes of white rice for shipment in July, a company spokesman said. The rice was bought from American Rice at $340 per tonne.

WHEAT TENDER - Guyana is tendering on Thursday for 2,300 tonnes of spring wheat, 1,000 tonnes of soft red winter and 3,000 tonnes of hard red winter under the PL-480 program, agents for the buyer said. Shipment was slated for July 4-26.

VEGETABLE OIL TENDER - The Egyptian state's Food Industries Company said it was seeking 20,000 to 30,000 tonnes of veg oils for delivery in July. The oil may be either raw sunflower oil, semi-refined cottonseed oil, U.S. cottonseed oil of 162 degrees or degummed soyoil. The company wants 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes for delivery in the first half of July and the same amount for the second half of the month.

RICE TENDER - The Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan (RECP) on Monday invited new bids for the sale and export of 5,000 tonnes of basmati variety Pak-7 1996/97 (July-June) rice containing seven percent broken. An RECP official said bids, to be submitted by June 16, had been reinvited after the corporation scrapped an earlier tender for the sale and export of the same quantity of basmati. He said the corporation felt the three bids opened on May 26 were too low at $436 per tonne FOB, $435.10 and $425.
BARLEY TENDER - Iran on June 9 will seek 100,000 tonnes of optional feed barley for September shipment, traders said.

CORN TENDER - Privatised Egyptian Starch and Glucose said it was seeking 10,000 tonnes plus or minus 25 percent, buyer's option, of yellow corn of Egyptian, U.S. or Argentinian origin. The firm said the deadline for bids was Thursday June 12.

VEGOIL AND TALLOW TENDERS - El Salvador seeks 4,500 tonnes prime bleachable summer yellow cottonseed oil in bulk and about 1,000 tonnes of sunflowerseed oil under the PL-480 export program for July 20-August 5 shipment. Offers are to be received by June 16. El Salvador also seeks on June 16 about 1,650 tonnes of tallow and about 800 tonnes of top white tallow. Shipment dates were set for July 20-August 5.

MARKET TALK - U.S. grain giant Cargill's shipment of 20,000 tonnes of wheat originally destined for North Korea is thought to be headed for southeast Asia or Sri Lanka after the collapse of a zinc-for-wheat barter, traders said Monday.
South Korean grain importers are seen taking a high profile this week as its biggest buyers re-tender for feed wheat and meal after passing on the purchases last week.
South Korean feed millers and crushers were seen eyeing nearby shipments of soybeans and soymeal this week following a sharp fall in prices in the world soybean market.
